body:
## Summary

Environment providers now accept resource specs, prepare existing backing inputs, and provision from an opaque preparation bound to the creating provider instance. Host-direct adopts the injected host runner through the provider lifecycle. Docker preparation uses held or published pinned digests and waits on ImageBuild rather than building Dockerfiles. Until #2731, controller-admitted baseline tags remain launchable: preparation resolves their local digest before provisioning.

```text
resource spec kind + provider instance
  → prepare(spec, admitted credentials)
  → instance-owned preparation
  → provision(id, preparation, runtime options)
  → runner, mounts and lifecycle handle
```

Placement policies freeze an explicit provider-instance metadata label into each created Environment; provisioning, adoption and backing recovery honor it. Runtime selection rejects ambiguous instances and removes literal runtime-name lookups. ADR 0058 records the #2874 ruling and the operator correction: ADR 0057 is the unrelated forge-observation decision and stays active.

Part A of the two sequential PRs requested by #2862. Part B follows with provider-owned caches, per-cache availability, ImageBuilder, metadata-only RegistryClient, opaque RegistryAuth and the runtime checker.

Closes #2862

## Evidence

- **Before:** image building was part of the generic provider trait, and host-direct readiness bypassed provisioning.
  **After:** both providers implement the same lifecycle; preparation ownership and unique kind/instance selection are exercised through injected collaborators. Failed host adoption cannot publish readiness.
- Baseline cut-over regression: the exact live fleet tag with no `image_build_ref` provisions by a resolved digest; controller and daemon tests cover new and legacy baseline provenance.
- Validation: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, the Git boundary checker, and all 10 checker tests pass. The workspace gate passed when run alone after transient executable-busy and broadcast-lag harness failures on earlier runs.
- Live acceptance is operator-run because this vessel has no Docker: `scripts/accept-environment-provider.sh /path/to/repo branch registry/repo@sha256:digest`. Use a public pinned image containing Git on a Docker host that enforces memory and swap limits. The script runs the existing checkout/discovery example through the provider trait and destroys the backing at completion.

### Mutation check

Two targeted mutants were caught by assertion failures and restored: refusing a valid host-direct spec (`environment_specs_select_exactly_one_kind`) and reversing ambiguous-instance rejection (`provider_selection_is_kind_and_instance_scoped`).

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way.

**Blast Radius:** provisioning.

Legacy checkout Dockerfile configs still decode, but admission now asks for ImageBuild and a pinned output digest. The repository’s unsupported active `.flotilla/environment.yaml` is retired as `.flotilla/environment.yaml.legacy`; the crew-image guide names the migration. Existing ImageLayer Dockerfile fragments remain build inputs. Ordinary mutable registry tags are refused. Until #2731, baseline-sourced tags remain supported: new records freeze baseline provenance in metadata, and older records recover it from their owning Vessel’s placement policy. Preparation honors the pull policy and resolves the tag to a local digest; provisioning uses only that digest. Existing running tagged Environments stay running and are adopted as before. In-flight pending tagged Environments can launch when their baseline provenance is recoverable; legacy unlabeled pending records require the owning Vessel and its baseline policy to remain available. Stored image fields are not rewritten. Runtime-only interface changes require rolling the fleet together. Credential artifacts remain the existing mechanism in Part A; Part B replaces them with operation-scoped handles and centralized cleanup.

## Resource schema changes

No resource schema change. No out-of-repo resource author needs a companion update for this PR.

## CI coverage

Existing workspace jobs cover the injected provider and reconciler tests. No workflow changes or new runner types.
title: Reshape environment providers around preparation and lifecycle (Part A)
